newsitem.title: USA: U.S. says Primakov illness won't stop NATO talks.
newsitem.headline: U.S. says Primakov illness won't stop NATO talks.

text.p: Talks with Russia on a NATO charter with Moscow will continue despite the illness of Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov, the United States said on Friday.
Primakov underwent a gallstone operation on Friday and might be out of action for up to three weeks, Russian doctors said.

"First, we want to wish Foreign Minister Primakov a speedy and full recovery from his operation. Second, the negotiations with the Russian Federation continue," said State Department spokesman Nicholas Burns.

NATO and Russia are hurrying to complete a charter on their relations before a July summit of the Western alliance which will open the door for former Warsaw Pact states in Eastern Europe to apply for NATO membership.
Russian President Boris Yeltsin said in Germany on Thursday that the charter agreement would be signed on May 27 in Paris. But the United States says the document is far from complete.

The charter, which will give Moscow the right to close consultations with NATO on European security, is designed to compensate Russia for the absorption of its former allies into the Western alliance.
NATO's talks with Russia are led by Secretary-General Javier Solana, but Burns said U.S.-Russian meetings on the issue were "upcoming".
He gave no details, but Deputy Secretary of State Strobe Talbott has been leading the U.S. side in talks with Russia on the charter.
